scope_covered: Existing cfg(loom) model of the real refcount transition functions: the same generic up_ref/down_ref used by SSL_SESSION, X509 and X509_STORE, instantiated over loom::sync::atomic::AtomicI32 through the RefAtomic trait.

This is a model of the transition logic, not a hand-written simplification: the Loom module implements RefAtomic for loom's AtomicI32 and calls the production up_ref/down_ref.

s56_x509_cache_publication.why: The production transition logic is ossl_x509v3_cache_extensions: it takes (*x).lock through CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock (a pthread rwlock), builds CacheBuild, installs seven raw NonNull slots plus scalar c_ulong/c_long fields on a #[repr(C)] X509, and publishes with ex_flags|EXFLAG_SET. The unresolved race is that x509_vfy readers read crldp/nc/altname/akid/skid/ex_flags without any lock. Loom can model its own AtomicUsize/RwLock/UnsafeCell, but production has no loom seam for the C rwlock or for the plain field memory. A faithful model would require parameterising X509, its lock and every field access over loom types (a production change), not a toy re-implementation.
s56_x509_cache_publication.what_a_toy_would_hide: A hand-written model with an AtomicUsize ex_flags and a loom RwLock would prove a property of the toy, not of the code: the actual defect is the reader that takes no lock at all, and the C lock is outside Loom's control.
s56_x509_cache_publication.evidence: No Loom module exists for x509/v3_purp.rs; the only cfg(loom) module is runtime/refcount.rs.

s57_tls_session_bookkeeping.why: The unresolved obligation is a data race: eviction/removal/flush write (*c).not_resumable and (*c).owner and mutate the session payload under the context's CRYPTO_RWLOCK, while a thread that already holds a reference reads them with no lock. Those fields are plain (non-atomic) members of #[repr(C)] SslSession, and the lock is a C pthread rwlock; neither has a loom seam. The reference-count sub-obligation IS faithfully modelled: SessionRef lowering and the shared up_ref/down_ref use the RefAtomic trait, and the existing loom_tests instantiate the production functions over loom::sync::atomic::AtomicI32 and pass 4/4.
s57_tls_session_bookkeeping.what_a_toy_would_hide: A model of not_resumable as a loom::AtomicU8 would change the production representation and would not model the unlocked read of the actual field; it would answer a different question.
s57_tls_session_bookkeeping.evidence: runtime::refcount::loom_tests 4/4; no cfg(loom) module in ssl/ssl_sess.rs.

s56_s57_loom.conclusion: Loom can and does model the S57 reference-count transition logic, and it passes. It cannot faithfully model either unresolved obligation (S56 cache publication or S57 not_resumable/owner/payload bookkeeping) with the current code shape, so no toy model was produced.

matrix_establishes: Every instrument that ran was proven active by a deliberate failure on the same invocation path (Miri UAF under both borrow models; ASan heap-use-after-free; TSan data race; Loom concurrent-write causality violation; Kani false assertion FAILED; MSan use-of-uninitialized-value).
Miri: the 9-test admitted TCB suite and three focused owner/lifetime tests are UB-free under both Stacked and Tree Borrows for the executed inputs.
ASan: four focused owner/record paths are free of memory errors; one 84-byte error-state leak at thread exit is an open finding.
TSan: five concurrent refcount/store/certificate tests show no data race.
Loom: the production refcount transition logic is model-checked 4/4 over modelled atomics.
Kani: two pure bounded state/length invariants are proved for their full domains.
MSan: the instrument is active; two focused instrumented paths produced no diagnostic (a bounded observation only).
matrix_does_not_establish: S56 X.509 extension-cache publication safety against the documented unlocked x509_vfy readers: no Loom model, no concurrent test, and TSan did not exercise it.
S57 session-bookkeeping data-race freedom: no Loom model of the plain not_resumable/owner/payload fields, and no concurrent session-cache test exists.
Any full-library Miri/ASan/TSan result. Only named tests executed; 2196 lib tests were filtered out in the sanitizer runs.
Any BOUNDARY or SEAL gate, any SAFETY_DISCHARGED or SAFE_COMPATIBLE claim, any consumer graduation.
Any cryptographic, constant-time, authority-differential or compatibility result (these instruments do not measure those axes).
That the 84-byte ASan leak is or is not a product defect; it is recorded at its exact allocation site and requires adjudication.
ASN.1 pointer/length arithmetic: the Kani harness is UNSUPPORTED (internal compiler error), so no proof exists there.
Initialisation soundness across libc: MSan cannot instrument the system glibc, and no MSan control over that boundary exists.
non_claims: A green instrument run is not a safety certificate under the AGENTS.md FAST/BATCH/BOUNDARY/SEAL schedule.
A source-level clean result is not constant-time evidence.
Miri's borrow model is a research instrument, not the normative aliasing specification.
The temporary canaries were test-only, never present in a release configuration, and were reverted before this receipt was written.
